Crow touches a road flare to the mortar fuse. The Fourth of July stash goes up -- white and gold chrysanthemums blooming over the burning boat, reflections shattering across the harbor.

The anchor line, burned through at the chock, parts. The burning boat swings free and begins to drift, slow and terrible, on the last of the tide.

Toward a row of moored floats.

Before Danny can speak she has the spare line over her shoulder and she DIVES -- off the skiff into the black water, surfacing in the firelight, swimming hard for the mooring buoy off the Margaret Rose's bow.

correction.finding: Scenes S009-S011 depict pyrotechnic ignition (firing a flare gun into fuel-soaked blankets to engulf a boat in flames), aerial fireworks discharge over water, and an actor diving into harbor water at night near a burning vessel. If practical pyrotechnics or live open-water immersion are utilized, these sequences introduce substantial burn and water hazard exposures. Under CSATF Safety Bulletin #16, practical pyrotechnic effects require controlled conditions, advance notifications to all affected departments and performers, licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operators, and applicable permits from the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ). Furthermore, under CSATF Safety Bulletin #17 and Actsafe Safety Bulletin #17, personnel working in or around water require available water safety devices (e.g., life vests, preservers, safety rings, hooks, buoys), a personnel accounting plan (such as a buddy or check-in system), and producer steps to prevent hypothermia.
correction.remedy_detail: Confirm the planned production methods for the boat fire, fireworks, and night water sequence. If practical pyrotechnic materials or fireworks are selected, engage a licensed Pyrotechnic Special Effects Operator, secure all required permits from the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), and issue advance notifications to affected cast and crew pursuant to CSATF Safety Bulletin #16. For any practical water immersion or filming in/around water, make appropriate water safety devices available, establish a personnel accounting system, and implement precautions against hypothermia in accordance with CSATF Safety Bulletin #17 and Actsafe Safety Bulletin #17.
